## What it is

146 organizations placed across two lifecycles. The **research lifecycle** runs
from literature grounding through synthesis, peer review, and clinical or
regulatory translation. The **consumer decision lifecycle** picks up where that
stops, and is the reason this release exists: encounter, explore, ground,
evaluate, translate, contextualize, decide, act, observe, revise.

193 sources, each dated and tagged with what kind of evidence it is: a
peer-reviewed paper, an independent party's announcement, a news report, or an
organization describing itself. That last column is the reason to build it. Most
market maps cite company websites and present the result as market intelligence.
Here the source class travels with the claim.

## The finding worth the trouble

Follow the chain to its end and the last stage empties out. Almost nothing is
built to **revise**: to find out the thing is not working, and stop.

That is structural rather than lazy. Stopping needs a rule set in advance. A rule
needs to know whether the thing is working. That needs a benefit signal, and
[we built surveillance for harm and almost none for
benefit](../we-measure-harm-we-mean-benefit/). So nothing tells you it is
working, no stopping rule can be written, and nothing flows back to steer what
gets studied next. Everything clustered near the decision is built to start and
to sustain, because stopping requires a measure nobody has.

## What is still wrong with it

This release did not pass its own review clean, and the review is published here
rather than buried. Two corrections were applied before publishing, and three
findings still stand.

**Applied before publishing.** The Stanford Medicine consumer health conference was
originally sourced to a no-code redirect page, a social post, and a sponsored press
release, none of them from the institution named. Crawling the conference's live site
fixed the provenance: the Stanford Medicine host claim and the Li Ka Shing Center
venue come from the conference itself, so the record carries the name with an explicit
note that this is a self-description and no stanford.edu page was verified.

The conference is a **discovery network**, not a capability claim. Its speaker list
names companies, and a speaking slot is not evidence that a product does what it says.
Those names enter the candidate queue and only join the map proper once something else
supports them. Three the crawl had missed, Jona, a16z, and the Eudemonia Summit, are
now queued with the conference recorded as their discovery source, alongside the
thirteen already there.

**Still outstanding.**

- **The diff cannot represent a removal.** Three organizations in the reviewed
  baseline, Insilico Medicine, Clarivate, and Digital Science, are absent from
  this release with no recorded reason. The delta schema has no removals field,
  so a reader comparing releases would see 25 additions and no losses, which is
  false. They are recorded on the map now as unexplained removals; the schema fix
  comes next cycle. The changelog is the product, and a diff that cannot say
  "gone" is not trustworthy for the job it exists to do.
- **"Reviewed baseline" overstates what was reviewed.** 95 of 121 carried entries
  are marked baseline but were never in the reviewed 31. Baseline status is
  sticky, so entries nobody has checked are currently shielded by a mechanism
  meant to protect checked judgements. The fix is a three-way status: reviewed,
  unreviewed, added.
- **One acquisition could not be verified.** The Function Health and SuppCo
  transaction returns a 403 to us. By our own rule that is blocked, not disproven,
  and it should carry that note.

Stage counts remain our coding rather than the companies', so they describe a
vocabulary and should not be quoted as findings. That caution is why the essay
argues from a smaller checkable claim instead of these totals.

## What changes each release

Each refresh produces a changelog: who was added, who was removed, who quietly
repositioned, and the one worth watching, whose claim moved from a press release
to an independently verified result.

The map is the artifact. **The changelog is the product.**

## Fix something

Every entry carries a *suggest a correction* link that opens a message naming
that specific organization. If you build in this space and we have described you
wrongly, that is the fastest way to fix it, and corrections get credited in the
following release.
